name: Myofascial Pain Syndrome
definition: Regional musculoskeletal pain attributed to painful muscle and fascia with taut bands/trigger areas, after excluding more specific neurological, inflammatory or structural causes.

typical: Pain with sustained posture or load

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is clinical; routine imaging is unnecessary.
investigations.MRI: MRI is only used when an alternative structural diagnosis is suspected.

green: Exercise, movement restoration and ergonomic modification
amber: Needling/injection techniques are adjuncts and should not replace active rehabilitation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Mamsa/Snayu Vata-type pain phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Regional musculoskeletal pain attributed to painful muscle and fascia with taut bands/trigger areas, after excluding more specific neurological, inflammatory or structural causes.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
